svg.text: From debate claims to testable models
Speaker attribution follows the transcript; model judgments remain independent scientific evaluations.
Mr. Kamkar claim/argument
Dr. Vahdati-Nasab objection/claim
Genealogy, migration, isolation & DNA
Models 01–11 + interactive continental explorer
Recent genealogical ancestry; rare migration can spread a founder lineage.
Ancient regional occupation, isolation, endogamy, and missing genetic signals challenge simple versions.
Models separate genealogical from genetic ancestry and make barrier timing explicit.
Key scientific output
Compatibility depends on reproductive connectivity; zero paths are hard impossibilities.
Livestock chronology • Model 12
“Eight pairs” linked to Adam-era animal appearance.
Domestication is not biological lineage origin.
Inserted-pair detectability • Model 13
Special pair inserted into an existing human population.
Why would an independent insertion match human genetics?
Agency & fine-tuning • Model 14
Stone-tool pattern recognition is extended as an analogy to cosmic fine-tuning.
Model judgment
Same Bayesian form, but archaeological calibration does not transfer automatically to cosmology.
Moral evolution & conformity • Model 15
Evolutionary/conformity account of norm-following and the “middle” majority.
Group acceptance cannot by itself define moral truth.
Descriptive norm dynamics are separated from normative justification.
Repository rule

A debate claim is not treated as established because a simulation can reproduce it. Each section asks what follows under explicit assumptions, then states what evidence would be needed to strengthen or reject the historical claim.
Speaker labels identify who advanced the claim or objection in the transcript; synthesized repository claims are labeled as synthesis.
